attrs.description: The accounts we speak as
Reach per client: a client's comments, discovery, DMs and invites run on its own logins (`clients.accounts.reddit`, `.linkedin`) into its own database
Comments as an event source
Cold outreach on social sites: a person's warmed account, paced
People on a platform
Find someone to follow by name or topic, on every site at once (Marketing → Feed): no link needed
Decide's comment source: drafted comments still waiting on him whose newest model draft has no decision yet, each with what the draft answers
People: a Reddit profile read into who they are
Places: subreddits where our buyers ask questions
Reddit read signed out: every call goes to autobrowse's `reddit-public` site, never to one of our accounts
What a subreddit asks of an account before our comment stays up
Threads: new posts in watched places, filtered in code, ranked by a model, the day's best queued with a researched draft in William's voice
Which account a draft goes out as
The model that drafts for reach, split by arm
The draft-model scorecard: for each model that wrote a reach draft since a date, how its drafts ended
DM drafts: the model writes our next message on a thread waiting on William (a reply to their last word) or to an accepted invite (a first message), kept on the contact (`draft`, `draft_for`)

Enroll: pick `new` contacts on a platform, give each the lightest active account, and queue the first thing to go: the invite (LinkedIn) or step 1 (Reddit), or propose the invite for his yes (`first: "proposed"`)
His comment decisions as few-shot examples
Follow-ups in a thread
DM follow-ups on the executor, as texts do (channel-sms/src/follow.ts)

Message and Invite from People: a person we hold (`li:<people.id>` with a LinkedIn page, `reddit:<handle>` read from Reddit, `linkedin:<vanity>` seen only through a touch) becomes a reach contact (`found_in = people`) on first use
His own picks, by link (Outreach → Engage, the paste box)
Drafted invite notes: the model writes a short note on a proposed LinkedIn invite while the account's free notes last this month
LinkedIn invites from our own people
Outreach's day caps (William, 10-26): follows a day per platform, each on the shared warm-up ramp from its first follow
When approved comments go out: one account's lane, spaced, inside waking hours in its zone, under a cap a day
Pain points line
Engage's Pass: he's done with a person (not a lead, not worth a reply, spam)
How much each account may do today: one settings object, and the pure checks the loop runs against it
Comment proofs: what to check for a sent item, and the `comment_proofs` row each check overwrites
His calls on a post (comment, like, follow, skip) and the likes and follows sent with no yes
The model's comment for a post, guarded against made-up claims, and its redraft
Comments on others' posts on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and Threads
Code's rank of a post: the audience's world, growth, who wrote it, timing; job ads are off
The platform reads: each site's posts as one `FeedPost` shape, through autobrowse as the account
Each platform's comments settings block (`<platform>.comments`), its limits and defaults
The pass's search words: his own by yield, rested when they find nothing, and the model's new ones

DMs as console records for the Marketing app: each person's thread (`marketing.dm`), each template slot William writes (`marketing.dm_copy`), with what the preview needs to draw them, each comment on our posts (`marketing.comment`), each LinkedIn invite (`marketing.invite`), and the people we can write to from Outreach → People (`marketing.person`)
Our own no (bad input, an opted-out person, an empty template): an answer, not an outage
Replies in: each account's new inbound, one row per platform id (the unique index dedupes), the contact marked `replied` and its queued steps skipped
Reply boxes when he writes replies himself (`drafts.replies` = you)

What the three objects share: `ReachDeps` as the worker wires it, a client's own copy of it (`clientDeps`: its logins' rows, its keys), the channels an account sends through (`channelsFor`), the wake to the watch, and a site's refusal that never retries
`ReachDesk`'s accounts: the list, one added, its state, its health now
`ReachDesk`'s comments: answered in their thread, read again, armed, DMed, dropped
`ReachDesk`'s contacts: finds, one added, the list, enrich, enroll, and the sequence templates

The context of `ReachDesk`: the request shapes several handler groups share, and `deskContext(deps)`, the closures they all use (one invite, the terminal map of a refusal, the clock, a client's database, the sender's nudge, one comment answered)
`ReachDesk`'s LinkedIn invites: the pass, the proposed, his yes and no, a withdrawal
`ReachDesk`'s People: a person drafted, messaged, followed or invited, and a DM from an Engage row
`ReachDesk`'s posts to comment on: the comment, a like or follow, passes, skips, redrafts, the list, the pass now
`ReachDesk`'s schedule: drafted comments onto spaced slots, and off them
`ReachDesk/settleSend`: a person's word on a send autobrowse could not call
`ReachDesk`'s numbers: the draft models' scorecard and the reach stats
`ReachDesk`'s DM threads: the list, one thread, read, a reply queued for the sender
`ReachDesk`: the operator's reads and writes (accounts, finds, enrich, enroll, templates, threads, comments, invites, posts, schedules), each one journaled
Reddit discovery on Restate: `RedditReads/wren` reads signed out (autobrowse `reddit-public`, paced and capped by the desk)
Cold outreach on Restate:  - `ReachSender/fleet`: the send loop
A send that lands at most once, on Restate
ReachDesk.paste: a link he pastes in Outreach → Engage (`../intercept.ts`)
`CommentProofs`: each sent comment checked at 2 minutes, an hour and a day (`scheduleProofs`, called by the send handlers), or now by hand
Scheduled comments: the slots `scheduled.ts` keeps in `send_at`, each fired as a ReachDesk call delayed to its slot
`ReachSender/fleet`: the send loop
`ReachWatch/daily`: reads each account's inbox on the warm cadence (`@wren/core/warm`): every 2 minutes right after a touch, easing to 30
Approved comments on a schedule: each drafted, queued comment gets a slot on its account's lane (`pacing.ts`), kept in `send_at`
Cold outreach on Reddit and LinkedIn: three tables, each one fact
The send ledger: one row per item that must land at most once
Outreach copy: William writes every word
The policy from `WREN_REACH_*` settings

A person settles an unsure send: he saw it on the site, so it is recorded as sent the way a send records it (the item's state, a touch, the draft record), he asks for it again, or he drops it: it did not go out and he does not want it sent
William's words for the slots sequences.ts declares, kept in the template store (`@wren/core/templates`, kind dm, system `reach`): every save a version, the live one what goes out
The operator's reads: threads, one thread, counts
The send tick, in steps a journal can bracket: every database move is one step (`run`), every platform call sits between two of them
The outreach tables as touches: one function per source row, called where the row is written and again by the backfill, so both keep the same line under the same ref
